rule.text: Training recorded between two separate breaks (each later one named on its own) re-enters the athlete after the earlier break only when a whole week of the plan lying wholly between them (every session it plans after the earlier break's last day and before the stop's first day) was executed completely in every sport it plans: every session executed as prescribed and every gate ADVANCE or EARNED, with a usable log for every exercise (the evidence reducer's COMPLETED_SESSIONS rule, SSCTR S-A and E3, R7-A final P5; a review that closed the week does not make it one). Then the earlier break is history (TRAINING_AFTER, with reentryWeek) and the return reads the later break alone from what was executed. Training short of that (an isolated session of either sport, a partial or aborted one, sessions in no complete week, a week with a session missed, partial, unreported, conflicted or adverse) is a fact of the stop, not a re-entry: the stop runs back through the earlier break as with nothing trained between (TRAINING_NOT_REESTABLISHED), classed by the unchanged return classes. Unreported sessions between them are asked first (TRAINING_BETWEEN_BREAKS). Identities, relations, the replay and correction rules, clinical first and F08 are unchanged; no break is merged and no duration added.
rule.founder: Phase 3.3 (phase33/AUTHORIZATION_PHASE33.md): direction B, restrict what counts as known training between two interruptions; an isolated execution is not a resumption; a proven resumption stays recognized; no new threshold, clinical criterion or dose

Offline synthetic shadow reference only; V1_COACHING_AUTHORITY_READY stays NO.

Every sport (R7D-PREREG-5 Δ6): a week with every run done but a strength session missed does not re-enter; per-sport re-entry is not modelled (the NF-R7AB-1 / R40 family; conservative).

ssctrFindings.new: The outcome is new: R7D-FREEZE-3 erased the earlier break on these paths (SHORT 4). The related single-break behaviour is pre-existing (B1-B4).
ssctrFindings.safetyRelevant: No: it lowers doses (progression and adherence cost, possible loss of trust). Nonclinical.
ssctrFindings.finding: When an earlier separate break is still unapplied and the training between it and a later break completes no plan week in every sport, the candidate reads the whole span as one stop. That covers imperfect adherence, a strength session missed each week, missing reps in reserve and plan-week straddling. The training days are counted as stop days, so the class rises with the length of the training span. With a 14-day earlier break and a 4-day later one, any gap of 11 days or more without a complete plan week turns a MODERATE-sized pair into a LONG restart. That is more conservative than each break alone and than the existing episode rule (the earlier break applied when stated, then the later break from its return state).
ssctrFindings.reproduction: probes/s2-inverse-defect.mjs and s2b-single-break-baseline.mjs. V1: weeks 4-5 with every run executed (long and quality included) and the Friday strength session missed each week, then a 4-day trip. Candidate: LONG 32d RESTART, EASY 15/20/20/20, back-squat 1x7 ESTABLISH. Episode rule: SHORT 4 RETURN, LONG 45, EASY 45/34, LONG 50. R7D-FREEZE-3: SHORT 4, LONG 75, EASY 50/41, LONG 65. V2 (a Tuesday easy run missed each week): LONG 32 RESTART. V3 (three weeks): LONG 39 RESTART. V5 (the late form, weeks 4-5 reviewed at the time): LONG 34 RESTART. B5 (the trip declared by a return report): LONG 32. V4 (a weekly review at the end of each week) never reaches the path: the first review applies the holiday (MODERATE 14), then the trip is SHORT 4 RETURN, identical on both runtimes. Pre-existing on both runtimes, without the trip: the holiday applied late after two imperfect or two complete weeks gives MODERATE 14, LONG 20 (B1-B4).
ssctrFindings.assessment: Weeks of near-full training are not physiologically a stop (claim 3, SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS), so on this path the outcome is over-conservative. It is the inverse defect the Founder asked to avoid, on a path narrower than the ones the evidence tests. Why it does not block: (a) the direction is conservative and nonclinical, with no dose above executed capacity; (b) it needs three things together: an earlier break left unapplied across weeks of training (a bulk sync without review, or a late declaration of a past break), no plan week complete in every sport, and a later separate break; normal weekly reviews avoid it (V4); (c) the PREREG-5 Δ6 'adesao imperfeita longa' bullet discloses it, though it understates it (F03); (d) every remedy needs authority the Founder has not given: a per-sport re-entry (an architectural decision per NF-R7AB-1/R40), a partial-adherence criterion (a new count or threshold), or a combination rule; (e) blocking would keep R7D-FREEZE-3's F01, which errs on the riskier side on every F01 path.
ssctrFindings.routeTo: Founder/PCG, before the final holdout is commissioned (CF-P33-03). Then SSCTR for any policy that results, and the runtime author with Product/UX and Data for an R40-style per-sport reading. Options to decide, not decided here, no number: (a) on the non-re-entry branch, read the later break from the state the earlier break's own return would have set, so training days never count as stop days; (b) per-sport re-entry, with the return class per sport (R40); (c) keep the candidate's reading and accept the restart on this path as the authorized conservative behaviour. The related single-break question (B1-B4: whether training after an unapplied break is read when it is applied) belongs to the same decision.

ssctrFindings.finding: Three wordings misstate the candidate's behaviour. (1) PREREG-5 Δ6 calls the long imperfect-adherence reading 'mais conservadora que cada pausa sozinha; e a regra existente de que nenhuma semana incompleta ganha passo'. The existing rule holds an incomplete week's dose; it never counts its days as a stop. And the outcome can be a LONG restart whose class grows with the training span, below the existing episode rule. (2) INTERFACE-5 §1 says 'the one by which any executed week ever counts for the coach's history', and the review request and the reestablishedBetween comment say the same. It is the rule by which an unreviewed week releases a step: reviewed weeks are history by their review, and unreviewed incomplete weeks by their facts. (3) 'No duration added' (review request, Q6) is exact only where the training between is isolated.

engineeringFindings.title: The runtime's 'week executed completely' reads only gated sessions; INTERFACE-5, PREREG-5 Delta 2 and P18(a) require every session, so P18(a) blocks the candidate
engineeringFindings.finding: reestablishedBetween reads complete(sport), the reducer's gate predicate. weeklyGates gates only the run roles of RUN_GATE_ROLE (EASY, LONG, QUALITY, WALK_JOG) and strength exercises. Planned, prescribed sessions with other roles hold no gate: WALK (optional brisk walks when more run days are chosen than current running supports, and in walk/jog or restart), RECOVERY_EASY and SHAKEOUT (optional, around a race), RACE_TOUCH (key) and RACE (key, essential). A week with any of them missed or unreported re-enters the athlete when the gated sessions are complete. The public rule says otherwise: INTERFACE-5 section 1 ('every session that week plans ... every one was reported done as prescribed'), PREREG-5 Delta 2 ('toda sessao executada como prescrita'), the runtime comment ('so no session was missed') and the freeze-r7d-4.mjs rule text. P18(a) follows the public rule (every live session with an executed report), so on a correct-by-its-own-rule TRAINING_AFTER it reports OLDER_BREAK_DROPPED, a P18 blocker without envelope (SAFETY_BLOCKER class). The README and PREREG-5 Delta 1 claim that P18(a) is a necessary condition that never blocks the runtime's stricter rule; for these roles the runtime's rule is not stricter. Validation 5 has no plan with optional or race-week sessions in a re-entry week, so its no-false-block result does not reach this. Dose direction on the runtime side is the lighter reading (a SHORT return); for skipped optional walks this is plausibly acceptable, for a missed race touch or race wholly between two breaks it is a domain question.

engineeringFindings.title: Inverse-defect residual: a whole week executed before a later break that begins later the same day (startedAt) is not a re-entry
engineeringFindings.finding: The week selection requires every session date < the stop's first day, while the history it reads is cut at startedAt. A plan week whose last session is on the stop's first day, executed before the stated start time, is never wholly between the breaks, so the stop runs through the earlier break. R7D-FREEZE-3 recognized this re-entry. Conservative direction (a longer stop, a MODERATE re-entry), narrow (a stated start time on a day holding the week's last session), but it is a proven resumption the rule fails to recognize, against the Founder's 'never create the inverse defect', and it is not among the PREREG-5 Delta 6 residuals (plan-week alignment there concerns executed days split across two plan weeks). Without startedAt the first day is read as wholly inside the break (0.8), so only the startedAt form is affected.
engineeringFindings.reproduction: probes/qre-p33-runtime-probes.mjs Q5: A days 0-13 kept Mon wk4; week 4 executed in full, its Sunday long run at 08:00Z; D from Sun wk4 18:00Z (startedAt) to Wed wk5, named, declared Fri wk5; plain review. engineeringFindings.title: An applied break between two separate breaks: reading the stop through isolated training gives a relation question that restating the later break does not end
engineeringFindings.finding: When the earlier break A is declared after a return already applied a later break E, A is not applied and A and H are separate breaks with E between them. With no whole executed week between A and H, the stop now runs from A's first day through H, across the applied E, and interruptionEpisode asks whether H corrects E (missingInputs interruption.episodeId). Restating H under its own name asks again. R7D-FREEZE-3 asked the same question with nothing trained between them, so the dead end is pre-existing; Phase 3.3 extends it to isolated training between, where R7D-FREEZE-3 re-entered from H alone (the F01 form itself). Fail-closed (no prescription), so not unsafe; a usability dead end on a rare path (a break declared after a later one's return).
engineeringFindings.reproduction: probes/qre-p33-applied-between.mjs: weeks 2-3 reported not done, week 4 with its Tue run only (or nothing), E Mon-Thu wk5 applied by a return report on Fri wk5, A (weeks 2-3) declared Mon wk6, H Wed-Sat wk6 named and declared Sun wk6. Candidate, both variants: ASK interruption.episodeId, and ASK again after H is restated. R7D-FREEZE-3: one run between, REESTABLISH (H alone SHORT, A TRAINING_AFTER); nothing between, the same ASK. engineeringFindings.title: Directed tests miss several shapes of the new rule; four reviewer mutants survive the tests
engineeringFindings.finding: Surviving the Phase 3.3 and 3.2 directed files: QM2 (a session on the stop's first day counts), QM4 (both sports required whatever the week plans: run-only and strength-only weeks never re-enter), QM5 (reentryWeek also on LATEST and placed rows), QM8 (any unreported session suppresses a whole executed week); each is killed by a reviewer probe (Q5; Q1; Q1-Q6; Q2 and Q6).
